node.name: wind_farm_ops_router
node.description: Decide what the control room or field staff member needs from the operations desk.

conditions.a: Is the user reporting a fault, trip or alarm on a specific turbine?
conditions.b: Is the user asking to schedule planned maintenance or an inspection for turbines?
conditions.c: Is the user asking about the status or progress of an existing work order?
conditions.d: Is the user requesting a safety permit or lockout authorisation to climb a turbine?

examples.msg: Turbine 14 tripped about ten minutes ago with a pitch system error and it won't restart.
examples.why: turbine trip with error code is a fault

examples.msg: Sorry if this is a silly question, but do you know if grapes are dangerous for dogs? I think mine ate a few and I'm a bit worried.
examples.why: pet health question, unrelated to wind farm

examples.msg: Good morning, I hope the shift is treating you kindly. We were going over next month's calendar and it seems the gearboxes on the northern row are due their yearly look-over, so I wondered whether we might pencil that in for the second week, whenever the crew has room. Many thanks.
examples.why: wants yearly gearbox check put on calendar

ctx: Hello there, last Tuesday I logged the yaw motor problem on turbine 7, I believe it was job 4417.
Thanks, I can see job 4417 for turbine 7 here. What would you like to do with it?
examples.msg: Oh lovely, thank you for finding it so quickly. I was really just wondering how far along that one is, the site manager asked me this morning and I didn't quite know what to tell her.
examples.why: asks progress of the found job

examples.msg: yo anyone catch who won the freaking derby last night, the whole group chat is losing it
examples.why: sports chit-chat, unrelated

node.name: oil_delivery_slot_reply
node.description: Classify what kind of information the customer's reply gives to the agent's last question.

conditions.a: The customer picks one of the delivery slots the agent has just offered.
conditions.b: The customer states a specific delivery date or day of their own choosing.
conditions.c: The customer provides their customer account number or invoice reference.
conditions.d: The customer says they do not know the answer to the question asked.
conditions.e: The customer refuses to give the information the agent has asked for.
conditions.f: The customer gives the current reading of their tank gauge or fuel level.

ctx: need a top-up on the tank before this cold snap hits
Sure. Before I book it, can I take your date of birth for security checks?
examples.msg: nah no way, not handing my birthday out over some chat, hard pass on that one
examples.why: refuses to give date of birth

ctx: Before we book the delivery, what is the capacity of your tank in litres?
examples.msg: I honestly have no idea, the previous owners put it in and never left any paperwork.
examples.why: does not know capacity; not a refusal

ctx: We have three slots next week: Monday morning, Wednesday afternoon or Friday morning. Which one suits you?
examples.msg: the middle one's good for me
examples.why: chooses offered Wednesday slot

ctx: To find your account, could you give me your customer number?
examples.msg: Oh, of course, I have the last invoice right here on the kitchen table, my husband always keeps them in a little folder by the bread bin. It says HO-55182 at the top, I believe that is the one you need. Thank you ever so much.
examples.why: reads out customer number from invoice

ctx: hi, tank's getting pretty low, can you send someone out
Happy to. What day would you like the delivery?
examples.msg: the 14th works, i'm home all day
examples.why: names own delivery date

node.name: roofing_request_router
node.description: Decide which kind of request the roofing customer is making.

conditions.a: The customer wants a repair booked for active damage on a roof we did not install, such as a leak, missing tiles or storm damage.
conditions.b: The customer wants to claim under our warranty because work we previously installed has failed or shows a defect, like leaking flashing or lifting shingles.
conditions.c: The customer wants a quote or estimate for a new roof or full replacement, including pricing questions or a site visit to measure up.
conditions.d: The customer wants to cancel a scheduled appointment or job entirely, calling it off rather than moving it to another date.
conditions.e: The customer wants to move an existing appointment or job to a different date or time, keeping the job itself in place.

ctx: Good afternoon. Our house is about thirty years old and the shingles have started curling badly.
Thank you. Would you like a quote for a full replacement, or should we send someone to patch the worst areas?
examples.msg: The full replacement, please.
examples.why: chooses quote for full replacement

ctx: Hello, thanks for contacting us. What can we do for you?
examples.msg: Last night the wind take many tiles from my roof and now water is coming in the bedroom. Roof is old, other company make it twenty years ago. Please somebody come to fix.
examples.why: needs repair, roof not ours so not warranty

examples.msg: Third storm this month and now there's water dripping through my damn kitchen ceiling. Some old tiles blew off. I need someone out here today.
examples.why: storm leak needs repair

ctx: Hi Ms Carter, a reminder that our crew is booked to replace your gutters and flashing this Thursday at 8am. Does that still work for you?
examples.msg: Oh, Thursday's no good anymore, could the men come the week after instead?
examples.why: moves booked job to later week

ctx: hey, you guys put a new roof on our place back in 2022
Thanks for letting us know. What can we help with today?
examples.msg: so the ridge vent you put in is already peeling up and letting water in, figured that should be covered
examples.why: failure of their own install, covered

examples.msg: don't bother finding us a new date, just scrap the whole damn job, we ain't doing the roof anymore
examples.why: explicitly not rescheduling, calling job off

node.name: gallery_collector_router
node.description: Decide what a collector contacting the gallery is asking for.

conditions.a: The collector asks about the price, availability or purchase terms of a specific artwork, for example whether a piece is still for sale or can be reserved.
conditions.b: The collector wants to arrange a private viewing or visit to see works in person, including choosing a date or time to come to the gallery.
conditions.c: The collector asks for background on an artist or a work, such as provenance, technique, exhibition history or the artist's biography.

examples.msg: hey, so I've got a painting from my grandma I'm thinking of selling, do you ever take on works from private owners?
examples.why: wants to consign a work; no candidate covers

examples.msg: I'd like to come in and look at the large blue canvas from the Mira Holst series before I make up my mind. Could I book a time on Saturday?
examples.why: books visit to see work

ctx: Good evening. I attended your opening on Friday.
Thank you for coming. How may I help you?
examples.msg: I was quite taken with the small bronze by Tomas Varga near the entrance. Could you tell me whether it is still available and what the asking price is?
examples.why: asks availability and price of piece

examples.msg: random one but do you know if it's going to rain tomorrow?
examples.why: weather question, unrelated

ctx: Those three works are only on display until Sunday. Would you like to see them in person, or should I send you more photos?
examples.msg: first one, hell yeah, pics never do this stuff justice
examples.why: chooses seeing works in person

ctx: Thanks for your interest in the Elena Sorvik landscape. Would you like the price list, or would you rather hear about where the piece has been shown and who owned it before?
examples.msg: The second, please.
examples.why: chooses exhibition and ownership history

node.name: consignment_confirmation
node.description: Decide how the seller responds to the consignment summary they were asked to confirm.

ctx: To summarise: one oil painting, estimate 3,000-5,000, reserve 2,500, seller's commission 15%, entered in the March sale. Shall I confirm?
examples.msg: Hang on. What exactly does that 15% even cover? Nobody bothered explaining it and I'm not signing off blind.
examples.why: asks what commission covers before deciding

ctx: Hello, I bring the silver tea set to you last week.
Yes, here is the summary: silver tea set, estimate 800-1,200, no reserve, April sale. Shall I confirm?
examples.msg: Excuse me, my neighbour is knocking on the door now, I need go and see who is it. One moment.
examples.why: interruption unrelated to the consignment

ctx: Here is the summary: two porcelain vases, estimate 4,000-6,000, reserve 3,500, May sale. Would you like to go ahead, change anything, or withdraw them?
examples.msg: forget it, the last one. I've had enough of this
examples.why: picks withdraw option

ctx: Summary: a Victorian writing desk, estimate 1,200-1,800, reserve 1,000, June sale. Please confirm.
examples.msg: Fine, yes, that's all correct, go ahead. Took long enough to get here.
examples.why: agrees the summary is correct

ctx: hey so about the clock i dropped off
Sure. Mantel clock, estimate 600-900, reserve 500, February sale. Shall I confirm, or would you rather withdraw it?
examples.msg: the second one, my sister wants it after all
examples.why: chooses withdraw

ctx: I'm calling about the watercolour I left with you.
Here is what we have: watercolour landscape, estimate 400-600, reserve 350, January sale. Can I confirm this?
examples.msg: I really can't let it go for anything under 500, to be honest.
examples.why: implies raising the reserve

node.name: production_office_router
node.description: Decide what the crew member needs from the production office.

conditions.e: Add someone to the call sheet

ctx: Hi, I'm helping out on the shoot on Harbour Street on Saturday.
Great, thanks for pitching in. What do you need from the office?
examples.msg: I'm bringing my van with all the food things and I've got no idea where I'm meant to leave it all day.
examples.why: needs a place to leave van

examples.msg: The 24-70 came back off B-cam with a cracked front element and the follow focus gear is stripped. Needs logging before it goes back on the truck.
examples.why: logs cracked lens and broken gear

ctx: hey, we're scouting spots for the chase scene
Sounds fun. What can I sort out for you?
examples.msg: we wanna shoot on the old bridge on Kent Road next Tuesday, can you get us the council's ok for that?
examples.why: wants council permission to film there

examples.msg: yo settle this, who the hell invented the hot dog, me and the boys been arguing for an hour
examples.why: trivia argument, unrelated

ctx: Hello, I am the gaffer for the night scenes next week.
Hi, welcome aboard. How can the office help?
examples.msg: I need reserve two more big LED panel and one haze machine for the Thursday. Also the parking near studio was very full today, but is not so important.
examples.why: reserves lights; parking is aside

node.name: parish_office_router
node.description: Decide what the person contacting the parish office wants.

conditions.a: Is the user asking to arrange a baptism or christening?
conditions.b: Is the user asking to hire the parish hall for an event?
conditions.c: Is the user requesting a pastoral visit or a conversation with a priest about a personal matter?
conditions.d: Is the user asking about the times of services or Mass?

ctx: Hi, we've just moved into the parish.
Welcome! How can the office help you?
examples.msg: Our daughter was born in June and we'd love to get her christened sometime in the autumn. Also, is the car park open on weekdays?
examples.why: wants daughter christened; car park aside

ctx: Good morning. My mother has been a parishioner here for forty years.
Good morning. What can we do for you?
examples.msg: She has been confined to her bed since a fall in March and very much misses the comfort of the church. She often speaks of Father Okonkwo.
examples.why: housebound mother implies priest visit

ctx: Hello, St. Brendan's parish office. How can I help?
examples.msg: I'm organising my dad's 70th and wondered if the hall is free on the 12th of next month. Lovely flowers at the entrance, by the way.
examples.why: wants hall for birthday party

ctx: Hello, I've been meaning to get in touch for a while.
examples.msg: I retired recently so my Sundays are completely free now, and I sang in a choir for thirty years before my voice got tired, so I do miss it.
examples.why: hints at wanting to sing in the choir; not covered

ctx: Hello, parish office. Are you calling about service times, a hall booking, or something else?
examples.msg: Oh, the first one, sorry, I think. I just really don't want to get it wrong.
examples.why: chooses service times

node.name: costume_hire_router
node.description: Route incoming messages from theatres and schools to the right costume hire queue.

conditions.a: Hire ext - extend return date on live order
conditions.b: New hire enq - avail + quote for a production
conditions.c: Returns - book collection/drop-off of hired stock

examples.msg: Hello, you know how I make the bread more soft? Every time it come out very hard.
examples.why: baking question, unrelated

ctx: Hi, we hired the Victorian costumes for our school play.
Thanks. What can I help with?
examples.msg: The play went so well they've added two more nights next weekend, so we'll still need everything.
examples.why: extra shows imply keeping costumes longer

examples.msg: hey, any chance we can hang on to the pirate stuff for another week? oh and the hats were a massive hit with the kids, by the way
examples.why: keep current hire longer; hats aside

ctx: Hello, it's Lakeside Drama about order 2231.
Hi, I have your order here. What do you need?
examples.msg: We won't need the extra week after all, the show closed early. When can we bring everything back?
examples.why: no extension; wants to return stock

examples.msg: panto in december 12 dame outfits you got any how much
examples.why: new production, asks stock and price

node.name: restoration_intake_reply
node.description: Classify what kind of answer the owner gave to the restorer's last question.

conditions.a: The owner gives a date or time window for collecting or bringing in the item.
conditions.b: The owner says they do not know the answer, for example the item's age or origin.
conditions.c: The owner chooses one of the treatment options the restorer has just offered.
conditions.d: The owner declines to share the information the restorer has asked for.

ctx: chair leg snapped need it fixed
We can either glue and dowel the original leg, or turn a new one to match. Which would you prefer?
examples.msg: original one keep it
examples.why: picks repairing original leg

ctx: I'd like to get my grandmother's clock restored.
Lovely. Do you know roughly when or where it was made?
examples.msg: It's been in the family since before I was born and there's no label or mark on it anywhere.
examples.why: implies no knowledge of age or origin

ctx: Good morning, I wish to have a painting cleaned.
Certainly. For our insurance form, could you tell me what you paid for it or its current valuation?
examples.msg: I would rather keep that between myself and my insurer, if you do not mind.
examples.why: withholds valuation

ctx: I've got a cabinet that needs some work.
Happy to help. Can I take your home address so we can arrange a collection?
examples.msg: I'd prefer not to give my address out, thanks. I can bring the cabinet in myself.
examples.why: refuses to give address

ctx: hi, got an old mirror with a gilt frame that's flaking
We can help. Do you know if the gilding is original water gilding or a later repair?
examples.msg: honestly cant tell, id have to ask my aunt, she had it before me
examples.why: does not know; would have to ask someone

ctx: Hello, I'm the one who emailed about the walnut bureau.
Yes, thank you. When would be a good time for our van to collect it?
examples.msg: Oh, how kind of you to ask. Well, my daughter is visiting the week after next so the house will be chaos, but any weekday morning next week would be perfect, I'm always up early with the dog anyway. Thank you so much.
examples.why: gives next-week mornings for collection

node.name: funeral_request_triage
node.description: Classify an incoming family request by urgency and category.

conditions.a: Urgent: a death has just occurred and the family needs immediate collection or transfer of the deceased, for example a death at home or in a care home today.
conditions.b: Time-sensitive: changes or details for an upcoming funeral in the next few days, such as readings, music, flowers, the order of service or notices.
conditions.c: Routine: paperwork or administrative questions with no deadline pressure, such as extra death certificate copies, invoices or pre-planning documents.

ctx: Thank you for calling. Is this about a loved one who has just passed away, or about arrangements already in progress?
examples.msg: The first one. I'm sorry, I don't really know what I'm meant to do next.
examples.why: chooses just-passed option

examples.msg: Good afternoon, I do hope I am not bothering you. My late husband's service was lovely, back in the spring, and I am only now going through his things. The bank has asked for another copy of the death certificate and I wondered if you might be able to send one, whenever is convenient.
examples.why: extra certificate copy, no deadline

examples.msg: I think the order of service has my mum's name spelt wrong and the funeral is on Friday, sorry, I'm panicking a bit
examples.why: error in upcoming service printout

ctx: Good morning, Hartwell and Daughters. How may we help?
examples.msg: Good morning. My father's funeral is on Wednesday and the family would like to add a second reading to the service. Could that still be arranged?
examples.why: adds reading to funeral this week

examples.msg: Could I get two more certified copies of my father's death certificate? The funeral was back in April, so there's no rush at all.
examples.why: routine paperwork; only urgent options offered
